0x0000001E.Name: KMODE_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
0x0000001E.Description: A kernel-mode program generated an exception which the error handler did not catch.
Recommendations: Check for recent driver updates or rollbacks
Run hardware diagnostics, especially memory test
Check system file integrity with SFC /scannow
Run chkdsk to verify disk integrity

0x0000007E.Name: SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
0x0000007E.Description: A system thread generated an exception that the error handler did not catch.
Recommendations: Update drivers, especially graphics, storage, and network drivers
Reset overclocking to factory settings if applicable
Check for hardware issues with diagnostic tools
Restore system to earlier restore point

0x00000050.Name: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA
0x00000050.Description: Memory corruption in the nonpaged area of memory, often indicating hardware issues.
CommonCauses: System service that has corrupted the memory
Recommendations: Run a memory diagnostic like Windows Memory Diagnostic or Memtest86+
Update BIOS and device drivers
Check for proper seating of hardware components
Disable any recently installed third-party services

0x00000116.Name: VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE
0x00000116.Description: The display driver failed to respond in a timely fashion. Usually occurs when the GPU hangs.
Recommendations: Update graphics drivers to the latest version
Check GPU temperature under load
Disable GPU overclocking
Test with a different graphics card if possible

0x0000009C.Name: MACHINE_CHECK_EXCEPTION
0x0000009C.Description: Hardware reported a fatal error to the CPU, usually indicating CPU, memory or power issues.
Recommendations: Check system temperatures and cooling
Reset BIOS settings to default or disable overclocking
Run memory diagnostics
Update BIOS to latest version

0x00000101.Name: CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT
0x00000101.Description: A processor thread failed to respond to a clock interrupt within the expected time.
Recommendations: Verify CPU cooling is adequate and fans are working properly
Remove any CPU overclocking and return to stock settings
Check the power supply for stability issues
Update BIOS to latest version

0x00000124.Name: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR
0x00000124.Description: A fatal hardware error occurred that the Windows Hardware Error Architecture reported.
Recommendations: Return all hardware to stock/default settings
Update BIOS/firmware to latest version
Run a memory diagnostic tool to check RAM
Monitor CPU and system temperatures

0x0000003B.Name: SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION
0x0000003B.Description: An exception happened in a system service, often related to drivers or system files.
CommonCauses: Third-party system utilities with kernel-mode components
Recommendations: Update all drivers, especially recently updated ones
Run System File Checker (sfc /scannow)
Run DISM tool to repair Windows image
Scan for malware with updated antivirus software

0x0000000A.Name: IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
0x0000000A.Description: A kernel-mode process or driver attempted to access a memory address it shouldn't have at the current IRQL.
Recommendations: Update drivers, especially recently updated ones
Run memory diagnostics tests
Check for malware with updated antivirus software
Disable recently installed software or drivers

0x000000D1.Name: DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
0x000000D1.Description: A driver tried to access an address while at an IRQL that was too high.
Recommendations: Update the driver mentioned in the stop code parameters
Check for memory hardware problems with diagnostics
Disable recently installed software or services
Boot in Safe Mode to isolate the problem

0x0000007A.Name: KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR
0x0000007A.Description: Windows cannot read data from the disk into memory. Usually disk or memory related.
Recommendations: Run chkdsk to check for disk errors
Check physical disk connections
Test memory with Windows Memory Diagnostic or memtest86
Update storage controller drivers

0x0000001A.Name: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT
0x0000001A.Description: A severe memory management error occurred in the Windows kernel.
CommonCauses: Incompatible memory timing settings in BIOS
Corrupt system files related to memory management
Recommendations: Run a comprehensive memory diagnostic tool
Remove overclock settings on RAM in BIOS
Update BIOS to latest version
Reseat RAM modules or try different memory slots

0x000000C5.Name: DRIVER_CORRUPTED_EXPOOL
0x000000C5.Description: A driver has corrupted a disabled executive pool, often indicating a serious driver bug.
CommonCauses: Memory corruption due to hardware issues
Recommendations: Update all drivers, especially third-party ones
Check for hardware-related problems, particularly RAM
Run System File Checker (sfc /scannow)
Test with a single memory module if multiple are installed

0x0000000F.Name: SPIN_LOCK_NOT_RELEASED
0x0000000F.Description: A kernel-mode process failed to release a spin lock, usually due to a driver issue.
Recommendations: Update drivers, especially for storage and network devices
Update BIOS/firmware to latest version
Check for hardware issues, especially CPU cooling
Disable any third-party filter drivers or utilities

0x00000019.Name: BAD_POOL_HEADER
0x00000019.Description: Memory pool header is corrupt, often caused by driver issues or memory corruption.
Recommendations: Update or rollback recently updated drivers
Run memory diagnostics
Temporarily disable antivirus software to test
Run System File Checker (sfc /scannow)
